summary: Fixed the validate-artifact.sh call-arity bug (extracted a shared skill_validate_task_artifacts helper into skill-base.sh, wired into command-gate-out.sh) and the forbidden "completed" status vocabulary in skill-orchestrate Stage 8 and Stage MT-5 (changed to "implemented"). Both fixes demonstrated live against a disposable fixture; documentation updated to establish return-metadata-file.md as the single normative vocabulary source.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed the validate-artifact.sh call-arity bug in command-gate-out.sh by extracting a shared skill_validate_task_artifacts helper into skill-base.sh, eliminating the spurious [FAIL] File not found line and making the artifact link-repair leg run for the first time. Fixed skill-orchestrate's two forbidden "completed" writes to .return-meta.json/.return-meta-multi.json (Stage 8 clean exit, Stage MT-5 exit_status), making gate-out's defensive status-correction branch for operation=orchestrate reachable for the first time. Both fixes demonstrated live against a disposable fixture (positive and negative control runs). Established return-metadata-file.md as the single normative status-vocabulary source, cross-referenced from handoff-schema.md and command-gate-out.sh instead of being independently restated.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent system, command-gate-out.sh's operation=orchestrate defensive status-correction branch reads .return-meta.json's status field and only proceeds for the accept-list {implemented, researched, planned} (never "completed", which is forbidden in that file's vocabulary per return-metadata-file.md). If a skill writer emits the state.json-vocabulary word "completed" into .return-meta.json by mistake, the branch silently never fires — it is not an error, just a permanently-skipped no-op. To verify such a branch is actually reachable, build a disposable fixture, desync state.json, write a status matching the accept-list via the FIXED writer's own jq snippet (not hand-authored), and confirm the diagnostic echo line appears; then re-run with the old/wrong value as a negative control to prove the fix (not something else) caused reachability.

Bash arity bugs in non-blocking ("|| true"-suppressed) call sites are easy to miss because they never surface as a failure — they surface as a misleading side-channel message instead. In this codebase, validate-artifact.sh's <path> <type> --fix contract was called as validate-artifact.sh "$task_dir" --fix (missing the type argument), so "--fix" silently bound to the type positional and the directory bound to artifact_path, producing a `[FAIL] File not found: <dir>` on stdout that `2>/dev/null` could not suppress, while `|| true` swallowed the actual exit code. The fix pattern: extract ONE shared per-directory-sweep helper function into the shared library (skill-base.sh) rather than trying to patch the inline call, so the correct 3-token form is enforced structurally at a single call site instead of hand-copied.
